svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.23.2.4 Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.2.4 Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood

g.text: Connector: Z550 hot-dip galvanized to ASTM
Wood treated with SBX (DOT) or zinc borate,
in a dry interior: uncoated carbon steel

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as provided in Sentence (3), connectors in
contact with preservative-treated wood are made
of
(a) hot-dipped, zinc-coated galvanized steel with a
coating weight not less than Z550 conforming to ASTM
A653/A653M, (b) a material that provides an
equivalent level of corrosion protection, or (c)
stainless steel.
Fasteners used to attach these connectors are
made of
(a) galvanized steel coated with zinc in accordance
with ASTM A153/A153M, or (b) a material that
provides an equivalent level of performance and is
compatible with the connector.
Connectors and fasteners in contact with wood
treated with SBX (DOT) or zinc borate and
installed in a dry interior environment are
permitted to be uncoated carbon steel.
Interior construction, including sill plates, not in
contact with the ground but exposed to occasional
sources of moisture, is a dry interior environment.
Drawn: generic hanger and angle, no make or model. Galvanized steel light grey, uncoated steel dark grey, treated wood green.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.2.4. (page 9-166)
